claim_evidence.beat: Dwayne Johnson and Jason Statham's on-screen chemistry "blossomed out of nowhere" during the filming of The Fate of the Furious.
claim_evidence.supporting_passage: It was great working with Jason, because we were really leaning into chemistry that kind of blossomed out of nowhere. We have worked together, obviously, in [Furious 7]. In [The Fate of the Furious], we were putting our scenes together

claim_evidence.beat: During The Fate of the Furious, Dwayne Johnson ad-libbed a line to Jason Statham that made Statham break character laughing, and that take was used in the movie.
claim_evidence.supporting_passage: So anyway, I remember in Fast 8, I thought, “Let me try this.” I said, “I just want to say something to you and talk shit in this scene, and you react how you react.” So, he said, “Okay, mate. Sure.” And I said, “I promise you. Trust me, I'm not gonna hang out to dry. If it works, it should be kind of funny.” We’re in the scene, and I remember specifically saying, “When this is over, I'm gonna knock your teeth so far down this road, you're gonna stick a toothbrush up your ass to brush them.” He looked at me and started to crack up. He broke his character, he laughed, and that’s the take that we used in the movie.

claim_evidence.beat: After The Fate of the Furious, Universal audience-tested the movie and "loved our characters together and loved what we were doing."
claim_evidence.supporting_passage: And it was after that movie that Universal said they [played the] movie back, audience tested it and loved our characters together and loved what we were doing.

claim_evidence.beat: This positive audience reaction was the "creative inroad" that made sense for the Hobbs & Shaw spin-off.
claim_evidence.supporting_passage: And that was the creative inroad we needed that made sense for the spin off. And then we made Hobbs and Shaw.
